title: Lightning technical sell + objection lane (rough)
content:
Purpose:
Quick reference for platform sellers to run a 3-slide / 3-minute technical sell, plus an objection lane for common deployment and economics questions. Rough WIP — meant to be printed as a single page cheat-sheet or used as speaker notes for a 5–8 minute customer call.

TL;DR (elevator):
- 60s: Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable latency and cost across hosted, dedicated, and private deployment modes. We help engineering teams move from model experimentation to production with observable SLOs, intelligent routing, and cost controls.

Target persona / meeting context:
- Primary: Platform engineers, infra architects, ML engineers evaluating managed inference for product launches or consolidation.
- Secondary: Product leads + procurement for reserved capacity discussions.
- Best use: First technical discovery or pre-demo alignment call where you need to be crisp on tradeoffs.

Three-slide narrative (speaker notes):
Slide 1 — Problem & signal (30s):
- Signal: teams running LLMs in prod hit unpredictable per-token costs, throughput bottlenecks, and silent quality regressions.
- Quick examples: spikes at index-time search, expensive embeddings batch jobs, or chat app tail latency during peak.
- Note to seller: open with customer-specific signal (if known): "we heard X is slow/costly".

Slide 2 — Redwood approach (60s):
- Unified runtime + smart routing — same API across hosted/dedicated/private.
- Cost levers: batching, prefix caching, quantization suggestions. Show 2x–6x token-cost savings examples (from our bench).
- Reliability: fallback model variants, cross-region routing, and SLA-for-dedicated.
- Ops: per-route observability, token-level cost breakdown, and eval-driven quality alerts.
- Demo hook: "I can show a 3-step demo of route fallback + cost trace in the console."

Slide 3 — Outcomes + next steps (30s):
- Outcomes: predictable latency SLOs, 20–60% unit-cost reductions depending on workload, faster rollout confidence (canaries + rollbacks).
- Next step options: pilot on hosted with sample load, reserved-capacity estimate for peak X requests/s, on-prem POC for compliance.

Objection lane (quick responses, belt-and-suspenders):
- "We can self-host; why Redwood?"
  - Short: You can — but Redwood buys you a proven runtime + ops that reduces months of infra tuning. Shipping time to safe production often >3–6 months; we compress that and provide SLOs and support.
  - Signal: mention dedicated customers who reduced infra ops headcount/tickets.

- "How do you keep costs low vs cloud GPUs?"
  - Short: smarter batching/prefix caching + quantization + routing to cheaper model variants. Real customers see 2x–4x reduction in per-token cost vs naive cloud-hosted endpoints.
  - Quick metric to offer: "on our customer sample, embeddings pipelines dropped from $0.25 to $0.07 per 1k units after caching and quant tuning." (callout: use exact pricing only when pre-approved)

- "Latency spikes/tail latency concerns."
  - Short: continuous batching with latency-aware policies + hot-key detection. We honor per-route latency SLOs and can isolate noisy tenants on Dedicated.

- "What about data security/compliance?"
  - Short: Private deployment (VPC/air-gapped) + KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. Offer a compliance pack and security review.

- "Model quality regressions after quantization?"
  - Short: Quantization profiles are workload-aware — we recommend and test per-prompt prompt sets and keep evals tied to rollouts. Canary traffic keeps production safe.

- "We need guaranteed throughput for X concurrent sessions."
  - Short: Reserved capacity (Dedicated) contracts with throughput sizing and burst options. We size by p99 tokens/s and simulated concurrency.

- "How do we handle vendor lock-in?"
  - Short: API abstraction allows you to pin model versions and swap under the hood; we avoid proprietary format lock-in and provide exportable deployment manifests.

Demo checklist (prep for 10–12 minute demo):
- Pre-demo: create a tenant route that points to two model variants (fast-cheap and default-high-quality).
- Show live: single request -> fallback from fast->default on QoS fail; show token-cost trace and latency trace in console.
- Show: per-route token cost and top prompt shards from observability.
- Show: canary rollout configuration and metrics streaming (60s view).
- Bring: customer sample prompt set if available (makes it stick).

Canary / fallback talking points (what to say during questions):
- Canary traffic split: start 1% -> 10% -> 50% with automated quality checks.
- Automatic rollback triggers: threshold on rollback signal (failed eval ratio, latency breach, or error %).
- Fallbacks: route to compatible model variant or cross-region instance when capacity constrained.

Pricing framing (quick scripts):
- Hosted: usage-based; emphasize fast time-to-value + fine-grained cost visibility. Use pilot credits to quickly show value.
- Dedicated: reserved capacity for predictable throughput; frame as insurance + lower unit cost at scale.
- Private: licensing + support for air-gapped/regulatory.
- Negotiation tip: for pilots, offer a time-bound reserved footprint discount in exchange for committed throughput forecast.

Useful scripts (copy/paste):
- 60s tech intro: "Redwood Inference gives you a single API to operate models across hosted, dedicated, and private modes. We give you observable SLOs, automatic fallbacks, and cost levers (batching, caching, quantization) so your production LLMs are predictable and affordable."
- Closing ask: "Can we run a 2-week pilot on a non-prod route with your sample prompts? We'll instrument and show two measurable wins: p99 latency and per-token cost delta."

Open questions / rough TODOs (WIP):
- Add 1–2 customer-specific metrics for each vertical (search, chat, embeddings).
- Validate the "2x–4x cost savings" wording with latest bench (ask research for last quarter numbers).
- Create single-slide visual showing cost path from no-caching -> caching -> quant -> dedicated. (Owner: Marcus) JIRA-INF-10122
- Decide whether to include concrete pricing examples in external facing deck (legal review). (Owner: Lina) JIRA-SALES-448

- This doc should become a one-pager + a 6-slide deck; current is cheat-sheet for sellers.
- Pull a short customer storytelling snippet from account "Vela Health" (ask CS) — helps with credibility.
